title: Fluconazole Ophthalmic Solution: Preparation & Clinical Utility
summary: Fluconazole (Diflucan) is a potent triazole antifungal essential for treating fungal keratitis and endophthalmitis, particularly against Candida and certain Aspergillus species. This guide outlines the precise compounding protocol, clinical indications, and management algorithms for ocular fungal infections.

sections.title: Clinical Indications
content: Fungal Keratitis: Particularly for Candida species.
Endophthalmitis: Prophylaxis and treatment for endogenous fungal involvement.
Alternative for patients intolerant to Natamycin or Voriconazole.

references.citation: Thomas PA. Fungal infections of the cornea. Eye. 2003.

sections.title: Compounding Protocol (0.2% Solution)
content: Step 1: Obtain sterile 2mg/mL Fluconazole intravenous injection solution.
Step 2: Utilize a laminar flow hood to maintain sterility.
Step 3: If necessary, dilute using artificial tears (preservative-free) to achieve the desired concentration.
Step 4: Dispense into a sterile, multi-dose ophthalmic dropper bottle.
Step 5: Label clearly with expiration (typically 7-14 days if refrigerated).

references.citation: Maharana PK et al. Mycotic keratitis: epidemiology, diagnosis and management. Indian J Ophthalmol. 2016.

sections.title: Contraindications & Red Flags
content: Do not use as monotherapy for filamentous fungi (Aspergillus, Fusarium) due to poor penetration and efficacy.
Monitor for signs of ocular surface toxicity with frequent dosing.
Significant liver enzyme elevation risk if systemic absorption occurs.

references.citation: AAO. BCSC Section 8: External Disease and Cornea. 2023.
Kanski JJ. Clinical Ophthalmology: A Systematic Approach. 9th Ed.
